logline: After mistaking small everyday oversights for proof that nobody notices her, a quiet café regular returns for a forgotten sketchbook—and finds a reason to stop hiding behind it.
story:
Every afternoon, Maya takes the same booth in a rain-streaked café. Across from her is an empty chair. Leo approaches with two cups out of habit, sees the empty seat, and takes one away. Maya watches the place where it almost landed.

She sketches people in her notebook: Leo wrestling with a crooked lamp, Max trying to shelter a paper bag from the rain. She tears the lamp drawing loose and slips it under her saucer. Looking down at the page feels safer than looking at them. When she raises a hand to order, Leo turns toward a crashing tray. When she starts to smile at Max, he looks down at his ringing phone. None of these moments is cruel. Together, they become the story Maya tells herself.

A gust through the opening door scatters Max’s receipts and loose coins. Maya helps him collect them. One receipt is soaked. She wraps his coins in a dry scrap from her sketchbook, leaving a tiny drawing of his ridiculous struggle with the wet bag on the outside. His phone rings again. He mouths a distracted thank-you and rushes out. Maya’s hand stays raised a moment after he has gone.

At her booth, she draws the empty chair again. She tears the page out, almost leaves it on the table, then folds it into her pocket. Leo lifts the lamp drawing from beneath her saucer along with the wet paper scraps nearby. Through the moving tray and cups, she sees what looks like the last of her drawing disappearing into a bin. She leaves before he can catch her eye. Her scarf slips across the seat, hiding the sketchbook she has left behind.

Outside, Maya reaches into her bag and finds no notebook. Through the café window, the empty booth looks like a small stage after everyone has gone home. She almost walks away. Then she spots her crooked-lamp drawing, flattened and taped beside the register. Beneath it sits her notebook, safe and dry.

Inside, Max stands at the counter, holding the paper wrapper she gave him. He is trying to show Leo the drawing, turning it the right way up with the awkward care of someone handling something important. Leo notices Maya and holds up the notebook: “I kept it dry.” Max looks from her to the drawing. “You made this?” Maya nods. For once, she does not immediately lower her eyes.

Leo gestures to a chair beside them while he finishes cleaning the counter. There is a tiny pause in which Maya could retreat to her booth. She pulls the chair out instead. “Can I sit here?” Max shifts his coat out of the way. Leo puts down a cup. Neither makes a speech. Nobody asks her to become a different person.

The café continues around them. Maya opens her sketchbook, then lets the pencil rest. Max is halfway through explaining the ruined paper bag with his hands. Maya looks up and listens. The final wide shot returns to the original booth: the chair across from it is still empty. Maya is simply no longer sitting there.
publishing_description: Have you ever felt invisible in a room full of people? Maya spends her afternoons drawing strangers in a café, convinced nobody notices her. A forgotten sketchbook gives her a reason to return—and a small chance to connect. Am I Invisible? is an original animated short about loneliness, mistaken assumptions, and the quiet courage of taking a seat. Featuring Maya, Leo and Max.

scenes.dramatic_change: The empty chair becomes a concrete image of Maya’s isolation.
scenes.action: Maya sits small in the booth. Leo approaches carrying two cups, notices the empty opposite seat and returns one to the tray. Follow Maya’s eyes to the bare circle where the cup almost touched. Her fingers tighten around her own cup.
scenes.camera: Begin on the empty chair across from Maya; low close-up on the second cup, then rack focus to her expression.
scenes.sound: Door bell, soft cup contact, rain against the window.
scenes.music: Sparse two-note felt-piano motif with room between notes.

scenes.dramatic_change: Maya wants contact but keeps choosing the safety of watching.
scenes.action: Maya sketches Leo adjusting a crooked lamp. She raises a hand to order; a tray clatters behind him and he turns away. She lowers her hand and continues the same line on the page, pressing harder, then tears the lamp drawing loose and slips it under her saucer.
scenes.camera: Close views of pencil, shoulder tension and lifted fingers; show the dropped tray in the same geography so the missed signal has a clear cause.
scenes.sound: Pencil drag, tray crash, a brief apology from background ambience without intelligible extra dialogue.
scenes.music: One motif note is left unresolved; no dramatic villain cue.

scenes.dramatic_change: An ordinary interruption feels personal to Maya.
scenes.action: Max struggles through the doorway with a rain-softened paper bag. Maya suppresses a smile and starts to look up at him. His phone vibrates. He looks down, missing her expression. Maya’s smile drains; she turns the page to a sketch of his wet bag.
scenes.camera: Medium view that holds both eyelines, then a restrained face close-up. Avoid repeated frontal talking compositions.
scenes.sound: Rain gust, paper rustle, a single phone vibration.
scenes.music: Soft low pad enters under the piano; keep the missed glance small.

scenes.dramatic_change: Maya actively helps instead of only observing.
scenes.action: Wind scatters Max’s loose coins and receipts. Maya crouches, gathers the coins into a dry paper scrap from her sketchbook, and folds it into a simple wrapper with her little wet-bag drawing showing. He accepts it, distracted by his phone, mouths thanks and hurries out. Hold her lifted hand after the door closes.
scenes.camera: Floor-level contact shots of knees, fingers and coins; shared two-shot for the handoff; hold her hand for a beat.
scenes.sound: Coins rolling, knees against fabric, dry and wet paper textures, door bell.
scenes.music: Let the score briefly brighten during the handoff, then recede without a comic sting.

scenes.dramatic_change: A mistaken interpretation pushes Maya to leave.
scenes.action: Maya sketches the empty chair and folds the drawing into her pocket. Across the café Leo lifts her lamp drawing and gathers wet napkins beside a bin, partly obscured by his tray; do not actually show him throwing away her drawing. Maya sees the motion and decides what it means. She stands, pulls her scarf free, misses the notebook beneath it and leaves.
scenes.camera: Show exactly what Maya can and cannot see. Insert the notebook remaining on the seat after she exits.
scenes.sound: Chair legs scrape, paper folds, her steps and the door closing.
scenes.music: The motif thins to a single sustained tone; leave silence after the door.

scenes.dramatic_change: She almost gives up the one thing she came back for.
scenes.action: Maya searches her bag for her sketchbook. She turns back, stops outside the rainy window and sees her familiar booth empty. Her shoulders drop. She begins to turn away, then notices the little drawing beside the register.
scenes.camera: Stay with her face reflected in glass; shift focus through the glass to the drawing. No magical transparency.
scenes.sound: Bag zip, wet pavement, traffic muffled behind rain.
scenes.music: Use rain and room tone alone for most of this beat.

scenes.dramatic_change: What looked like indifference is revealed to be incomplete information.
scenes.action: The lamp drawing is flattened beside the register. Max carefully turns the wrapper so Leo can see the sketch. Leo has placed Maya’s notebook away from the wet counter. Maya enters. Leo lifts it. Max recognizes the artist; Maya meets his eyes and nods.
scenes.camera: Over Maya’s shoulder for the reveal, then a wide triangle connecting the three people; close-up on the safe dry notebook.
scenes.sound: Door bell, paper flattening, notebook settling against a palm.
scenes.music: The original piano motif returns with one added answering note; no swelling climax.

scenes.dramatic_change: Maya makes a small voluntary choice to join them.
scenes.action: Leo gestures to an unused chair beside the counter. Maya briefly glances back toward her old booth. She sets down her bag and draws the offered chair toward her. Max moves his coat off the neighboring seat; Leo places a cup where she can reach it.
scenes.camera: Hold the pause before her decision. Track the chair’s weight and her seated contact; show hands supporting the cup naturally.
scenes.sound: Chair scrape, coat rustle, cup and saucer, a relaxed breath.
scenes.music: Warm but restrained harmony; leave space for the line and chair sound.

scenes.dramatic_change: The opening image changes meaning without pretending her life is fixed.
scenes.action: Maya opens her notebook. Max starts describing the ruined bag with his hands; she rests her pencil and looks up to listen. Leo straightens the lamp, now lighting all three. Return to the original booth and its still-empty opposite chair. Maya is no longer there.
scenes.camera: Intimate side view of the listening face, then a quiet wide match to the opening. End on the empty booth with the shared counter visible beyond.
scenes.sound: Ordinary café room tone, small friendly indistinct conversation without new intelligible lines.
scenes.music: Finish the motif simply; fade into room tone rather than a slogan or title card.

short_edit.story: Open on the almost-placed second cup and empty chair. Maya’s discouraged departure leads straight to discovering her drawing and notebook through the window. Show Max carefully unfolding her drawing, Maya choosing the offered chair, and the contrast with the now-empty original booth. Preserve enough of the paper-wrapper handoff as a brief insert that the reveal makes sense. Aim for roughly 45–60 seconds through a new edit, not by accelerating every long-form shot.
short_edit.ending: Maya puts her pencil down and looks up at the people beside her; return to her old empty booth to complete the visual question.
